claim_text: 1Password says an attacker gained access to some of its backend systems
summary: 1Password says: 'An attacker gained access to some of our backend systems and copied a limited amount of customer account information from a subset of our customers.'
detail: It says it began investigating on Nov 19, 2026, after indications that an attacker had gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: 1Password's own incident post states it; TechCrunch reports the same from the post.

claim_text: The attacker used an employee's corporate GitHub account to push malicious code to backend services
summary: 1Password says the attacker used the employee's account 'to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers.'
detail: It says the attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to its CI/CD system, which holds infrastructure secrets; it has rotated all credentials that may have been exposed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: 1Password's incident post describes the route in.

claim_text: How the attacker got into the employee's GitHub account is not known
summary: 1Password has not said how the attacker got into the employee's account. It says only that it 'revoked the stolen token'. TechCrunch says it is unclear, and that the company did not immediately answer its questions.
detail: 1Password also says it has tightened its GitHub, CI/CD and endpoint controls, which does not say what failed. In the Hacker News discussion, commenters guess at a hacked laptop or a stolen personal access token. Nothing public supports or rules out either.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources explains the first step in; the guesses come from commenters with no stated knowledge.

claim_text: No group has claimed the attack in anything we read
summary: Neither 1Password nor TechCrunch names an attacker or reports a claim of responsibility. TechCrunch says it asked whether the company had received any communication or demands from the hackers.
detail: We did not open leak or dark-web sites.
label: Not established

claim_text: Names, email addresses and account details of a subset of customers were copied
summary: 1Password says the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of users, including names, email addresses, account identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.
detail: The records also held public keys, Secure Remote Password parameters, tokens in certain invitation, provisioning and recovery emails, and other non-secret metadata. It says the public keys are public by design and the Secure Remote Password parameters cannot be used to get into an account.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: 1Password lists the data; TechCrunch reports the names and sign-in email addresses.

claim_text: 1Password says customer vaults and the keys that protect them were not affected
summary: 1Password says: 'Your vault data, the items in them, and the keys that protect them are safe and were not affected.' It says vault contents were at no time accessed by, or available to, the attacker.
detail: It says it does not store account passwords or Secret Keys, and that account recovery keys and its apps and browser extensions were not affected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company's own statement, repeated by TechCrunch. No one outside 1Password has checked it, so Reported.

claim_text: How many customers were affected is not known
summary: 1Password says only 'a subset' of customers. TechCrunch says the company did not say how many customers had information taken, or whether it had notified them.
detail: 1Password says the small number of users who had a pending invitation or recovery email during the incident have been notified. It has not said whether everyone whose details were copied is being told. BleepingComputer says it sent 1Password questions and had no reply when it published.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the three sources gives a number.

claim_text: 1Password says customers do not need to change anything and its services are working normally
summary: 1Password says: 'You do not need to update anything in your 1Password account' and '1Password apps and services are working normally.' It warns customers to watch for phishing emails about invitations or account recovery they did not start.
detail: It says it disabled the GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, rotated internal credentials, lengthened invitation and recovery codes from six digits to ten characters, and brought in independent experts.
label: Reported
notes: Nothing went down, so the story has no service state.

claim_text: 1Password says its apps and browser extensions were not affected
summary: 1Password lists '1Password apps and browser extensions' among the things not affected, and says the attacker's code was pushed to backend services. Nobody outside the company has checked.
detail: This is the main worry in the Hacker News discussion: an attacker who could change the apps, or the page where people sign in, could capture what a user types. 1Password's post does not separately name its website. It says it 'restored clean versions of the affected service'.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company's own statement, which TechCrunch repeats. No outside check has been published, so Reported.

claim_text: How the attacker's code got onto 1Password's servers is not explained
summary: 1Password says the attacker pushed malicious code to backend services, but not how it was deployed or whether it passed any review. It says it has since tightened its GitHub and CI/CD controls.
detail: Commenters on Hacker News say there was no code review or branch protection. That is a guess: 1Password has said nothing about either.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The post gives the route in but not the controls the code passed.

claim_text: The attacker also copied private source code and got into 1Password's build system
summary: 1Password says: 'The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system.' It says the code holds no user secrets, and that it is rotating every credential that may have been exposed.
detail: CI/CD is the system that builds and releases software. 1Password says it 'contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work', and that there is no impact on its services or product security.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: 1Password's own post states it; BleepingComputer reports it from the post.

claim_text: 1Password says the copied invitation and recovery tokens cannot open an account on their own
summary: 1Password says a token from an invitation or recovery email works only together with a single sign-on login or a code emailed to the user. It says it found no sign that any was used to take over an account.
detail: It says a small number of users had such an email pending and have been told, and that it lengthened the emailed code from six digits to ten characters so it cannot be guessed. BleepingComputer reports the same from the post.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The company's own account of how its tokens work. No outside check has been published, so Reported.

claim_text: 1Password says it will publish a root cause analysis in the coming weeks
summary: 1Password has added to its incident post: 'We will be providing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) with details in the coming weeks once our full investigation is complete.'
detail: It gives no date. The analysis is what would answer how the employee account was taken over and how the code was deployed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The line is at the top of 1Password's own incident post.
notes: Not in the post when it was first read on Nov 25.

claim_text: Canva is named by 1Password as a customer
summary: A customer story on 1Password's site says: 'Learn how Canva uses 1Password to strengthen sign-ins, accelerate global onboarding, and boost developer productivity with secure, streamlined credential management.'
detail: This shows Canva uses 1Password, not that it was affected. Canva has not said it was affected, and 1Password has named no affected customer.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: 1Password's own customer page for Canva says it uses 1Password.

claim_text: No organisation has said publicly that it was affected
summary: No company or public body has said its data was in what was copied, and 1Password has named no affected customer. It says only 'a subset' of customers.
detail: Where we looked on Nov 27: 1Password's incident post and its customer pages, SEC 8-K filings naming 1Password since Nov 15 (none about this incident), and reporting by TechCrunch, BleepingComputer, The Verge, Help Net Security and SecurityWeek (none names a customer). We do not search code or guess from other sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources names an affected organisation.
